title: Auto Runtime configuration file
description: The settings of Auto Runtime that are lists or maps, read from the file that CONFIG_FILE names. Each key stands for the environment variable of the same name in upper case, which wins over it. Secrets are written as references such as ${GATEWAY_API_KEY}.

allowed_origins.description: The origins a page in a browser may call the API from, such as https://app.example.com. ALLOWED_ORIGINS wins over it

name.description: The provider prefix, such as gateway in gateway/llama-3.3-70b: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, unique, and not a built-in prefix

base_url.description: The http or https URL that /chat/completions is appended to, such as https://gateway.example.com/v1

api_key.description: The key, sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>; in the configuration file a reference such as ${GATEWAY_API_KEY}

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, their values treated as secrets; in the configuration file a credential is a reference

query_params.description: Query parameters added to every request, their values treated as secrets

structured_outputs.description: true when the endpoint accepts response_format json_schema; otherwise JSON is asked for as json_object and the schema is only checked here. Default false

include_usage.description: Asks for usage in streamed responses. Default false

expose_provider_messages.description: true when the gateway's error messages are safe to show to callers of a reasoning function. Default false

allowed_provider_options.description: The top-level request body fields a reasoning function may set for this gateway through provider_options, such as user and metadata. Default none

model_gateways.description: OpenAI-compatible gateways, each a provider prefix of its own. MODEL_GATEWAYS wins over it

model_aliases.description: Model references a reasoning function may give, each sent on as another reference; a trailing * on both sides covers every model of a provider. MODEL_ALIASES wins over it

items.description: A model id as the provider receives it, such as eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0

declared_models.description: The models list_models shows for bedrock, bedrock-anthropic, azure, vertex and vertex-anthropic, which do not list their own, and for a gateway whose list cannot be read, keyed by the provider prefix. DECLARED_MODELS wins over it

items.description: A model reference a reasoning function may give, written provider/model, or provider/* for every model of a provider

allowed_models.description: The only model references a reasoning function may give, by name or through an alias, and list_models shows, each provider/model or provider/* for every model of a provider; every model when left out. ALLOWED_MODELS wins over it

type.description: mcp for a remote MCP server, given url; stdio for an MCP server this server starts as a process, given command; openapi for an HTTP API, given document. Taken from url, command or document when left out

url.description: The http or https URL of a remote MCP server, spoken to over Streamable HTTP

headers.description: Headers sent to a remote MCP server, or to an HTTP API outside its document's security schemes, with every request; the value of a reference such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY} is a secret, scrubbed from everything a call records, and a value written out is not

issuer.description: The issuer of the authorization server the credential was registered with, pinned: it is sent to no other. An https URL, or an http URL on a loopback address

client_id.description: The client id registered with that authorization server

client_secret.description: The client secret, as a reference such as ${GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET}

private_key.description: A private key in PEM that signs the client assertion, as a reference such as ${GRAPH_PRIVATE_KEY}

algorithm.description: The signing algorithm of private_key, such as RS256 or ES256

scope.description: The scopes to ask for, separated by spaces

auth.description: OAuth client credentials, for a server whose authorization server issues tokens to clients: client_secret, or private_key with its algorithm. An mcp server's authorization server is found from the server's own metadata, an openapi server's from the issuer's

command.description: The command of a stdio server: an installed, pinned program, never a package downloaded at start such as npx -y

args.description: The arguments of the command of a stdio server

env.description: The whole environment of the process of a stdio server, which inherits nothing else; the value of a reference such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY} is a secret, scrubbed from everything a call records, and a value written out is not

document.description: The OpenAPI document of an HTTP API, version 3.0 or 3.1, read once at start: an https URL, an http URL on a loopback address, or a path relative to the directory of the configuration file

base_url.description: The URL the calls of an HTTP API go to, in place of the first server its document names; required when it names none. An https URL, or an http URL on a loopback address

query_params.description: Query parameters sent to an HTTP API with every call, outside its document's security schemes, such as a tenant; the value of a reference such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY} is a secret, scrubbed from everything a call records, and a value written out is not

security.description: The credential of each security scheme of an HTTP API's document the entry gives, by the scheme's name, placed as the scheme says: an apiKey in its header or query parameter, a bearer as Authorization: Bearer, a basic as user:password; an oauth2 or openIdConnect scheme takes the auth block instead; each value is a reference such as ${BILLING_API_KEY} or ada:${BILLING_PASSWORD}, a secret, and one written out is refused

org.description: The org this server serves, a list of orgs, or * for every org of this server, required; one entry serves each org it names under one name, with one credential and one connection

playbooks.description: The playbooks this server serves within each org it names, by id; every playbook of each org when left out, and refused beside * for every org

allowed.description: The tools of this server a function may name, each named as the server lists it; every tool of the server when left out

record_content.description: Whether the arguments and the answers of this server's calls are kept whole, scrubbed of secrets, in the playbook's ledger, where anyone who may read the playbook reads them; false keeps their sizes alone. Default true

request_id.description: The response header, or for an MCP server the key of the metadata of a result, in which the server carries its own id of a request, recorded with each call

tool_servers.description: The tool servers whose tools a function may name, each bound to an org and optionally its playbooks: url for a remote MCP server, command for an MCP server run as a process, document for an HTTP API described by an OpenAPI document. Secrets are references such as ${GRAPH_API_KEY}. TOOL_SERVERS wins over it

people_may_add.description: Whether people may add connections through their agents; true when left out

allowed_hosts.description: The hosts a connection may reach, each a host or *. and a host for every host under it; every host when left out

credential_kinds.description: The kinds of credential a connection may take, of none, reference, secret and client_credentials; every kind when left out

variables.description: The variables of the runtime a reference credential may name, never one the runtime reads for itself; none when left out, so no connection takes a reference

issuers.description: The issuers of the authorization servers the client is registered at, each an https URL, or an http URL on a loopback address; one written with a placeholder, such as https://login.example.com/{tenant}, is kept as it is written

client_id.description: The client id the authorization servers issued

client_secret.description: The client secret, as a reference such as ${EXAMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET}

private_key.description: A private key in PEM that signs the client assertion, as a reference such as ${EXAMPLE_PRIVATE_KEY}

algorithm.description: The signing algorithm of private_key, such as RS256 or ES256

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint where the metadata of the authorization server leaves the choice; chosen from the client and the metadata when left out

registered_clients.description: The clients whoever runs the runtime registered at authorization servers, each with the issuers it is registered at, its client_id, and its client_secret, or its private_key with its algorithm, as a reference, or neither for a public client

connections.description: What people may add as connections through their agents, tool servers of an org which every playbook of the org may use, and the clients whoever runs the runtime registered at authorization servers. CONNECTIONS wins over it
